page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-96GB is a general-purpose cloud server belonging to the Cloud Native family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 20 vCPUs mapped to 20 physical cores with a single thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. System memory totals 96.0 GB, yielding approximately 4.8 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it does come with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance alongside weaker single-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU test ranks in the bottom 10%, whereas the multi-core CPU test falls within the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests show average read performance for both small and large blocks, though large-block write bandwidth is weaker, placing in the bottom 25%. Standard computational tasks, such as software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing, consistently achieve average tier results. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks also align with middle-tier performance expectations.

The shared CPU allocation presents a performance tradeoff, as reflected in the lower single-core benchmark scores. However, the high core count and 96.0 GB memory capacity offer a cost-efficient resource density for parallelizable workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated single-core execution. This server is suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or large-scale language model text generation, where text generation for a 7B model falls into the bottom 10% of performance.
